lead_headline: Restaurant intel surges with 4 new leads Sunday—C Burger smashburgers debut at McGregor Square, 303 Ramen sidelined by attic fire—while foreclosures cool to 33 filings, down a third week-over-week.

restaurant.blurb: 4 new leads today expand the active roster to 25 leads (11 openings, 14 closures). Fresh detections: C Burger (regenerative smashburgers from Half Eaten Cookie) launched at Union Station's McGregor Square this week. Wapos Cantina opened in Rosedale, replacing El Tepehuan with Boulder-chain tacos. Mendocino Farms debuted its third Denver sandwich shop at Union Station. Casualties: 303 Ramen in Regis sustained attic fire damage March 3, Powered By Besitos food truck shuttered permanently on West Colfax.

foreclosure.blurb: 33 new filings this week—down 33% from prior week's 49, marking second consecutive decline. Combined exposure: $11.1M, no filings above $2M. Highest case: $628K Douglas County property at 5118 Lumos Lane. 43 auctions queued for next seven days. Weld County maintains lead with 315 active cases, Arapahoe at 290. Two-week cooldown suggests filing pace normalizing after February spike.

reputation.blurb: 3 mentions yesterday bring the rolling seven-day count to 40 citations across 13 unique sources—unchanged total from prior week but representing entire tracking history. Denver Post remains dominant with 16 pickups, followed by Hoodline (5) and social platforms (Facebook, Instagram, X with 11 combined). Saturday highlights: Post's $9M Country Club home sale, Palantir's Denver-to-Miami relocation coverage, Hoodline's Golden Triangle landlord incentive story. Google News RSS captured 39 of 40 discoveries.

subscriptions.blurb: Net flat yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) holds March at +2 MTD (+0.3/day), while 90-day cumulative reaches +74 net. Weekend pause follows Thursday's −4 bleed and Friday's +2 recovery. Past fortnight reveals choppy water: Feb 24's brutal −9 day preceded a +12 four-day rally (Feb 25-27, Mar 1-2), but this week stumbled with back-to-back negatives (−1, −4) before stabilizing. YTD pace of +1.1/day still outpaces March's anemic run rate despite two-week volatility.
